s: Guarantees at-least-once event publishing by writing events to an outbox table in the same DB transaction as business data.
w: Instead of writing to DB then publishing to Kafka (non-atomic, can lose events), you write BOTH in one transaction: business row + outbox event. A relay (CDC connector, polling publisher, or log tailer) reads the outbox and publishes to the message bus. This eliminates the dual-write problem. Once published, outbox rows are archived or deleted. Combined with idempotent consumers, this guarantees at-least-once delivery.
use: Microservice event publishing where losing events is unacceptable
Replacing dual-write patterns (write to DB, then publish - race conditions)
Systems requiring transactional consistency between state changes and notifications
Any service publishing events to Kafka/RabbitMQ from database mutations
avoid: Already using CDC (Debezium) from WAL - CDC reads committed rows directly, no outbox needed
Fire-and-forget notifications where occasional loss is acceptable
High-volume event streams where polling overhead is prohibitive (use CDC instead)

pat.d: Atomic DB write + event eliminates dual-write inconsistency.

pits: Polling-based relay adding DB load at scale - migrate to CDC-based relay as volume grows
Outbox table growing unbounded - implement cleanup after confirmed publication
tips: Dual-write problem explanation is the core: DB write + message publish are two commits, not atomic
CDC vs polling relay: CDC is preferred at scale; polling is simpler to implement initially
